title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nvidia's Monday relief rally stalled Tuesday, with shares down 5.9% — now more than 10% below where they stood before Jensen Huang's resignation — dragging the Nasdaq down 1.5% and the S&P 500 down 0.5%, while the Dow rose 0.9%.

Markets: Short sellers who made roughly $13.7B betting against Nvidia last week gave back about 90% of those gains after Monday's Huang-driven surge; CoreWeave fell nearly 12% and Analog Devices dropped 17% on a weak profit outlook.

Markets: Brent crude slipped below $90/barrel, its lowest since late August, as Mideast supply fears ease and the IEA forecasts a Q4 surplus; US gasoline has fallen almost 70 cents over the past month to a $3.61/gallon average.
Companies: Anthropic shares fell 6.5% to $81.90, dropping below its $83 IPO price just over a week after its debut, even as broader tech rebounded.
Companies: AI-power plays rallied on Huang's return — Bloom Energy jumped 18% and GE Vernova also gained — while Databricks is reportedly in early talks to raise funds at a $225B valuation.
Companies: Nvidia drew a California AG subpoena over its China dealings and investor disclosures, adding to scrutiny even as Huang resumes the CEO role.

Macro/Policy: Trump personally pushed Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang, calling him "too big to fail," amid swirling (and contested) allegations about Huang's ties to a woman suspected of spying for China.

Macro/Policy: Axios scoop — insiders at OpenAI and Anthropic increasingly fear unreleased frontier models are too powerful to safely release, sparking internal debate over whether to keep training ever-larger models at all.
Macro/Policy: Wednesday's data docket includes the Q3 GDP estimate, October PCE (the Fed's preferred inflation gauge), and October new-home sales.
